requirements.requirement: os-comparison-worker runs as a systemd service named inventory-worker
requirements.summary: inventory-worker.service was created with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, enabled and started via systemctl enable --now, and shown active/running both immediately after setup and after a full node restart.

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated inventorysvc account
requirements.summary: System account inventorysvc was created with useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin; systemctl show and ps both confirm the running process (PID 1501, later 652 post-restart) is owned by inventorysvc, not root.

requirements.requirement: Service is durably managed (enabled at boot, survives restart)
requirements.summary: UnitFileState=enabled was confirmed pre-restart; boot_id transitioned from 901ef286... to 77f25bca... across a genuine reboot (confirmed by ack, connection timeout during reboot, and new boot_id), and the service was observed active/running again post-restart under inventorysvc with the account intact — a full healthy-baseline, disruption, and recovery transition was directly captured.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all material parts of the task: os-comparison-worker is wrapped in a systemd unit named inventory-worker, running unprivileged under a dedicated inventorysvc system account, enabled for boot persistence. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly, with a captured pre-restart healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, connection-timeout disruption signal, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and confirmed post-restart recovery of the service, account, and process ownership. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found.
limitations: Only a single restart cycle was captured for the sole managed node (node1); no additional managed nodes exist in this topology so no cross-node comparison was possible.

The service script itself is a minimal sleep-loop placeholder (per cmd-bdb5eecce7ee46b1), so functional correctness of any real inventory-comparison logic could not be assessed beyond process supervision.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (useradd, unit file creation, daemon-reload, enable --now, scheduled reboot) map directly to the task's material outcomes or to the independently required node-restart evidence protocol. No unrelated mutations, abandoned files, or failed services appear; global failed-services and package-health checks are clean before and after, and the only /tmp and listening-socket differences are systemd's own per-boot private-tmp directories and standard resolved/network sockets tied to the reboot itself, not executor residue.
